chunks: 'Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Kahili and Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him), who said:

Camphor is placed on the deceased at the places of prostration, and upon the labbah (throat-pit), and the soles of both feet, and the place of the sandal strap on the feet, and upon both knees, and both palms, and the forehead, and the labbah.

key_terms.الشِّرَاكِ: sandal strap — the thong of a sandal; its position on the dorsum of the foot marks a distinct camphor application point
key_terms.اللَّبَّةِ: labbah — the jugular notch, the hollow at the base of the throat between neck and sternum
key_terms.الْكَافُورُ: camphor — ritual purifying substance applied to the body of the deceased during funeral preparation
key_terms.مَوْضِعِ الْمَسَاجِدِ: places of prostration — the seven body parts that contact the ground in sajdah, given special status in fiqh

ai.seo_question: According to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in al-Istibsar, which specific body parts of the deceased receive camphor during Shia funeral preparation?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) specifies the exact bodily sites where camphor must be applied when preparing the deceased for burial. The sites include the mawadi' al-masajid — the seven body parts that contact the ground during sajdah (forehead, two palms, two knees, two toe-tips) — along with the labbah (jugular notch), the soles of the feet, the dorsal line of the sandal strap, and the knees and palms explicitly restated. The repeated mention of the labbah at both the opening and close of the list is noted by classical jurists and may reflect either textual transmission variants or deliberate emphasis.
word_analysis: the prostration points (body parts used in sajdah)
